law: One finite predication = one unit (master law §0), applied at comma-level granularity, not sentence-level. Concretely for this document: (1) asyndetic verb-initial continuation CUTS in this genre (A6) — this paragraph type is a chain of source sentences whose full stops were deleted, so يستخدم / يعرف / يتراوح / تشمل / أدت / كان / أصله each open a unit; (2) و + own finite predication CUTS (A1, non-negotiable here — my worst bleed), but و + bare noun/adjective NEVER cuts, which is why the long enumerations (والسلوك…وثقافة, التقسيم الطبقي…والانحراف, السياسيين…والأشخاص, فلكيا…ورجل دولة, مثل الصحة…ودور النشاط) stay whole; (3) حيث, في حين, لكن, ف clause-initial all CUT (A3, C2, B6, B1/F3); (4) the brake is weight, not syntax — a ≤5-word same-subject و-verb riding on the previous predication is absorbed (0b/0c).
reasoning: GENRE FIRST (checklist 1). This is running encyclopedic prose, not a list/table/MCQ, so the short-tail brake 0b is live and the I3/J1 one-item-per-unit rules are OFF. No cataphoric colon cuts either: تشمل (95), بما فيها (286), بما في ذلك (526) and بينهم من (226) are all announcers from the H1 list, but every one of them here rides inline inside a prose sentence with bare-NP items and no <NL> — that is the J5 configuration, not the H1 configuration, so I take no colon cut at 94-95, 285-286, 225-226 or 525-526. || BARE-NOUN RUNS. The 412-424 run is the one I re-checked hardest: N parallel same-type siblings with zero connectives is the I4 MCQ signal, but these are bare predicate nouns hanging off one كان in inline prose, so §0 wins over I4. || @67 (الاجتماعية, before يركز آخرون).
